prompt.context: Your client is AirCo, a U.S. airline that has significant operations at one of the Chicago airports. Due to cold weather, the client's planes often have to be de-iced, but because the need for de-icing is very unpredictable, the client decided to outsource the de-icing to IceCo last year. However, IceCo's performance has not been satisfactory. The client is considering in-sourcing airplane de-icing, but currently does not have enough resources to do the de-icing in-house. The client requires a 4-year payback on investments.
prompt.question: Should the client in-source or outsource the de-icing?

clarifying_info.q: What is causing IceCo's performance problems?
clarifying_info.a: IceCo is taking too long to de-ice the planes, leading to flight delays. We cannot quantify the financial impact of this.

clarifying_info.q: How many workers would be needed if we in-source?
clarifying_info.a: The client would need to hire 150 people for the whole icy season. The actual number of workers per month fluctuates and can get as high as 60. We have to pay workers for the whole month, even if we only need them for one week.

clarifying_info.q: How long is the icy season?
clarifying_info.a: There are 5 months in the icy season.

exhibits.title: Comparison of Outsourced vs. In-sourced De-Icing Costs
exhibits.shows: A table comparing cost components for IceCo (outsourced) and Client (in-sourced) side by side. The candidate is asked to complete and explain the second (Client) column.

exhibits.title: De-Icing Investment Costs
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the one-time investment costs required to in-source de-icing, broken down into three components: Equipment, Supplies, and Training.

framework: Cost comparison: outsourced (IceCo fees + chemicals) vs. in-sourced (labor + chemicals + one-time investment)
Payback period: calculate annual savings from in-sourcing and divide total investment by annual savings
Qualitative factors: IceCo performance issues (delays) that cannot yet be quantified
Recommendation: in-source vs. outsource decision with conditions/levers

questions.prompt: Calculate the in-sourced labor cost per de-icing event
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize that 150 workers are hired for the full 5-month season, determine a monthly figure, then divide by monthly events. Strong candidates note the inflexibility of monthly hiring contracts.

math.setup: Total events per season = 3,000. Events per month = 3,000 / 5 = 600. Workers per month = 150 / 5 = 30. Monthly labor cost = 30 workers x $4,000 = $120,000. Labor cost per event = $120,000 / 600 events.
steps: Events per month: 3,000 events / 5 months = 600 events/month
Workers per month: 150 workers / 5 months = 30 workers/month

questions.prompt: Calculate the total cost per event for outsourced (IceCo) and in-sourced (Client), then determine annual savings from in-sourcing
questions.guidance: Candidate should complete both columns of the cost table. Outsourced = fee + chemicals. In-sourced = labor + chemicals. Then multiply savings per event by annual event volume.

math.setup: Outsourced cost per event = Fee per event + (Cost per gallon x Gallons per event). In-sourced cost per event = Labor cost per event + (Cost per gallon x Gallons per event). Savings per event = Outsourced - In-sourced. Annual savings = Savings per event x Total events.
math.answer: Annual savings of $300,000 (Note: the casebook answer key uses $4/gallon for in-sourced chemicals giving $360/event and $140 savings/event and $420K/year — use the numbers as given in the exhibit table for the candidate-facing calculation)

questions.prompt: Calculate the payback period on the in-sourcing investment and assess whether it meets the client's 4-year requirement
questions.guidance: Candidate divides total investment by annual savings. Should clearly state whether the payback meets the client's 4-year threshold and what that implies for the recommendation.

math.setup: Payback period = Total investment / Annual savings.
steps: Using casebook figures: Annual savings = $140/event x 3,000 events = $420,000/year
7 years > 4-year requirement — does NOT meet the client's payback threshold
math.answer: ~7 years; does not meet the 4-year payback requirement

brainstorming.prompt: What levers could the client pull to either reduce the payback period for in-sourcing or improve IceCo's outsourced performance?

categories.name: Reduce in-sourcing investment costs
ideas: Lease equipment instead of purchasing it to reduce upfront capital outlay
Negotiate supplier discounts on supplies and chemicals
Phase the investment over multiple seasons

categories.name: Decrease in-sourced labor costs
ideas: Re-negotiate labor contracts for more flexible terms
Hire workers on a weekly or per-event basis rather than monthly
Use part-time or seasonal workers with variable scheduling
Automate portions of the de-icing process to reduce headcount

categories.name: Increase in-sourcing savings
ideas: Negotiate lower chemical prices through volume purchasing
Improve process efficiency to reduce gallons of chemical used per event
Increase number of de-icing events handled per worker per month

categories.name: Improve IceCo outsourced performance
ideas: Implement Service Level Agreements (SLAs) with defined performance metrics
Tie IceCo fees to meeting SLAs (penalties for delays)
Quantify the cost of flight delays caused by IceCo to add to the payback calculation
Dual-source de-icing to create competitive pressure on IceCo
Conduct regular performance reviews with IceCo management

recommendation: Based on the 4-year payback requirement, in-sourcing does NOT meet the financial threshold — the payback period is approximately 7 years, nearly double the requirement.
Therefore, the client should continue outsourcing to IceCo in the short term, while simultaneously pursuing actions to either improve IceCo's performance or improve the in-sourcing economics.
risks: IceCo's ongoing performance issues (delays) create unquantified costs in customer satisfaction, on-time performance metrics, and potential revenue loss — these could shift the decision if quantified.
Labor inflexibility (monthly contracts) is the primary driver of high in-sourcing costs; if more flexible arrangements are available, the economics could improve materially.
The $3M investment is a one-time cost; if the client's volume or season length changes, the payback period changes accordingly.
next_steps: Quantify the cost of flight delays caused by IceCo's underperformance to determine if those benefits tip the in-sourcing decision.
Negotiate with IceCo to implement SLAs with financial penalties tied to on-time de-icing performance.
Explore whether equipment can be leased rather than purchased and whether labor can be contracted on a more flexible basis to improve in-sourcing payback.
Revisit in-sourcing decision in 1-2 years if IceCo performance does not improve or if labor/equipment costs can be reduced.
